newsitem.title: RWANDA: UN refugee agency to meet on Rwandan refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN refugee agency to meet on Rwandan refugees.

text.p: U.N. aid officials will meet in in Geneva on Monday to decide whether Rwandan refugees in Zaire and Tanzania can continue to be treated as legitimate refugees, a senior U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees official said.

Assistant High Commissioner Sergio Vieira de Mello left the Rwandan capital Kigali for Geneva after a round of meetings aimed at finding solutions to the problems posed by the presence of over 1.7 million refugees in neighbouring Zaire and Tanzania.

The refugees, mostly Hutus, fled Rwanda in 1994 after the Hutu-led government was ousted by rebels of the Tutsi minority. Many refugees were involved in the government-led genocide of one million Rwandans, mostly Tutsis, and refuse to go home for fear of reprisals. Some 80,000 Hutus await trial in Rwanda.

De Mello said late on Saturday he had been asked by High Commissioner Sadako Ogata to assess the situation in Rwanda. After meeting Rwandan ministers, he said: "We all agree the non-resolution of the refugee problem is a major factor in the instability of the region.
"We need to take a different approach to the problem... implementation of the Cessation Clause is a possibility."

The Cessation Clause can be invoked if the U.N. agency considers that it is no longer necessary to accord refugee status to a group of people because the conditions which led to their exile have since stabilised in their country of origin.
"My own assessment is that a return to Rwanda would be safe," de Mello said. "But the problem of intimidation (in the refugee camps in Zaire) is huge."
Hutu hardliners hoping one day to regain power in Rwanda intimidate refugees in the camps to force them to stay in Zaire.
De Mello said an attempt to carry out a census of the refugees in the camps in Zaire recently had been frustrated by "violent sabotage".
"This is a challenge to our mandate," he added.
In Kigali, de Mello met diplomats whose governments control much of the donor aid given to the UNHCR.

Zairean Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda and Defence Minister Admiral Mavua Mudima are due to meet UNHCR officials in Geneva this week. Zaire has repeatedly called for the Rwandan refugees to return home, saying they have caused instability in eastern Zaire.

Rwandan Rehabilitation Minister Patrick Mazimhaka recently told Reuters that he believed many of the Rwandans in Zaire did not qualify as refugees. "They are criminals who committed genocide," he said.
The Rwanda government criticises the international community for funding the refugee camps which it says house the perpetrators of the 1994 genocide.
The funds spent on the refugee camps far exceed the aid provided to Rwanda itself, it says.
